summary: One live week since genesis (2026-08-28), and it was a full click-driven run of the Tibet mega-dam chain: chained, heat-scored on all 11 links, and given 4 scenarios in a single Saturday-morning burst. That's this week's real news. Everything else is quieter than it should be for a two-signal shop: `run radar` has never fired (both signals were hand-seeded by Ron at repo creation, zero new candidates found since), the AI-infrastructure chain's heat scores are still the original analyst priors from genesis day with no fetched-data refresh, the S2 screen's 8-name universe is 100% PENDING_DATA outside a VRT smoke test, `data/indicators.json` doesn't exist yet so no scenario check has ever been evaluated, and both routine registrations sit at UNREGISTERED in health/sessions.json even though this digest is now running — worth confirming the radar and digest triggers actually got wired on the claude.ai side. Read the Tibet chain items below; treat the AI-infrastructure item as a reminder to refresh, not a fresh finding.

ranked.title: Global hydro-equipment spillover — the chain's only money corner, and it's contested
ranked.case: This is the single most concrete finding to come out of this week's Tibet-dam chain build: Andritz, the Western hydro-equipment name least connected to Motuo in any public coverage, posted a record EUR 2.52B hydro order intake in 2025, a record EUR 3.6B group Q1-2026 intake led by hydropower, and a EUR 12.6B backlog up 20.5% versus year-end 2025 [Andritz results releases, 2026-03 to 2026-07]. The card's thesis is that a decade of Chinese domestic hydro demand absorbs Chinese supplier capacity (Dongfang/Harbin) right as the global pumped-storage cycle inflects, tightening exactly the market Andritz/Voith/GE Vernova sell into — and no beneficiary list anywhere connects the two. That scored impact 70 / crowdedness 30 / capture 65, UNDISCOVERED, money_corner true. But it isn't settled: a parallel session's independent heat pass scored crowdedness 44 instead of 30, arguing the Andritz backlog is already discovered by European institutional coverage — which would flip money_corner to false. That divergence is recorded honestly in the chain's notes and is unresolved. This is the one item worth a `run redteam`-style gut check or a first PCS pull on an Andritz-proxy ticker before you trust the corner claim.

ranked.title: Dongfang/Harbin hydro turbines — the obvious trade, with an unanswered H-share question
ranked.case: Dongfang Electric holds roughly 45% of China's conventional hydro equipment market and could see on the order of 54B yuan of orders from this project alone, with Harbin Electric as the other domestic heavyweight [CNBC, 2025-07-23]; Dongfang's Shanghai shares hit consecutive daily limit-ups on the announcement. Scored impact 90 / crowdedness 70 / capture 75, CROWDED — this is not undiscovered, it's the obvious equipment trade and everyone in China already owns it. The open question the card flags explicitly: the 54B yuan lands over roughly a decade, so did earnings estimates actually move in proportion to the announcement-day repricing, or did the stock get ahead of the numbers? The card names the H-share (1072.HK) vs A-share spread as the concrete screen entry point to answer that — worth putting on the `run screen` list for this chain.

ranked.title: AI-infrastructure power equipment — still the chain's money corner, but the scores are five weeks stale on genesis day
ranked.case: Transformers, switchgear, UPS, and backup generation scored impact 80 / crowdedness 38 / capture 72, UNDISCOVERED, money_corner true — the chain's own reference case for un-crowded-with-real-capture, built on multi-year transformer backlogs and record order disclosures across the electrical-equipment group [electrical equipment maker order disclosures, 2025-26]. The case for it hasn't changed since genesis and doesn't need re-arguing here. What does need saying: every heat score on this chain, including this one, is still the analyst-authored [INFERRED] prior from repo creation — the chain's own map_limitation note says as much, and no `run heat` refresh with fetched PCS data has happened since. VRT is the one name in the linked S2 screen with any real market data pulled (a smoke test, not a full screen run); the other 7 names in that screen — POWL, ETN, HPS-A.TO, GEV, ENR.DE, MYRG, CEG — are still 100% PENDING_DATA. This link earns its rank on the strength of the original case, not on anything new this week; it's ranked here as a flag to refresh, not a fresh finding.

ranked.title: Xizang Tianlu cement — real local pricing power, but already the most crowded name in the whole chain
ranked.case: The project implies over 16 million tons of cement demand into a region where hauling cement in is prohibitively expensive, giving Tibet-local producers genuine freight-protected pricing power; Xizang Tianlu was named the major beneficiary and was among the sharpest A-share movers on the announcement [CNBC, 2025-07-23]. Scored impact 80 / crowdedness 65 / capture 70, CROWDED — this is the retail-favorite dam trade inside China, the opposite of undiscovered. The card flags an open repricing question worth carrying forward: the A-share repricing was immediate on announcement day, but whether sell-side earnings estimates actually followed (the first leg of the repricing-lag test) is unverified because the free data stack doesn't reach domestic consensus figures. Flagged honestly as possibly-crowded-and-already-repriced rather than claimed as an edge.

ranked.title: Scenario S4 — Global hydro supercycle confirmation (25% probability) operationalizes the spillover thesis
ranked.case: This scenario is the mechanism by which the rank-1 money-corner claim would actually get confirmed or killed: pumped-storage and grid-stability demand plus Chinese capacity absorption push Western hydro equipment into a multi-year sellers' market with real pricing power, moving global-hydro-spillover UP LARGE and hydro-turbines UP MEDIUM. Its leading indicators are concrete and trackable — Andritz's own order-intake and backlog trajectory (already at the record levels cited above) and GE Vernova hydro-segment orders plus Voith capacity announcements — with an explicit invalidation sign (hydro order intake flattening for two consecutive quarters across the Western group). None of the indicators carry a machine-checkable `check{}` spec yet, so nothing here is armed for the weekday cron; they're read-the-earnings-call items for now.

ranked.title: S2 screen (power becomes the binding constraint) — the 8-name universe is built but essentially unscreened
ranked.case: The screen correctly identifies an 8-name universe across pure-play (VRT, POWL), picks-and-shovels (ETN, Hammond Power Solutions T3), second-order (GEV, Siemens Energy T3, MYR Group), and hedge (Constellation Energy) buckets, with tiers printed and the grid-EPC bid-competed-margin trap already named on MYRG. But every theme-revenue-exposure figure, every fundamentals line, and every crowdedness score across all 8 names reads PENDING_DATA — this is still the seed universe from genesis day, not a run screen result. Health line reads 8 examined, 0 fully scored, 8 pending, 0 errors. This is worth queuing a real `run screen ai-infrastructure S2` against fetched EDGAR and market data rather than treating the current file as a finished screen.
